newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest hogs seen $0.50-$1 lower Thursday - trade.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest hogs seen $0.50-$1 lower Thursday - trade.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hogs were expected to trade $0.50 to $1.00 per cwt lower Thursday, with lower cash pork prices and ample hog supplies likely to again weigh on hog bids, livestock dealers said.
Because of active marketings Wednesday and scaled back slaughter schedules, several dealers said they have much of Thursday's slaughter covered and a good share of Friday's.
However, some buyers for packers said several plants will be returning to normal slaughter schedules Thursday and many others will be back to normal Friday.

Hog prices have fallen steadily this week in reaction to sharp declines in cash pork prices, market sources said. The lower pork values prompted several major meat packers to scale back slaughter operations this week to protect operating margins.

USDA reported pork cutout values late Tuesday at $75.91 per cwt for Grade 1 carcasses, down from $81.46 a week ago. Top cash hog prices, basis interior Iowa, fell to $55.50 Wednesday from $58.00 Monday.
